This is a hedged, conditional aside embedded in a broader essayistic passage about children coming to resemble their aging parents, and it derives its positive charge entirely from Odette's already-scored preservation rather than giving Gilberte a distinct local outcome of her own, so it was not scored as a separate event.

The closing description of the princesse de Guermantes's salon as 'illuminé, oublieux et fleuri, comme un paisible cimetière,' where old family enmities have dissolved into new alliances, reads as essayistic reflection on the healing work of time rather than a direct evaluation of the princesse herself as hostess, so it was not scored as a status effect for her.
